This is not your typical, upscale Hilton, but a budget Vegas hotel hiding behind a positive brand name.  If you are looking for more affordable options, I would suggest checking into the Flamingo, Tropicana, Bally's, or something actually on the Strip. state: {"review": "Usually Mexican food served out of an outdated building with numerous building code violations is always the best. Not so much in the case of Carolina's. I arrived on a Saturday about 11 am to a short line and I had heard from one longtime Phoenix resident that this is the real deal. I had to try the famous tortillas right? So, I ordered up a cheese quesadilla and a red machaca burrito. How does it end up that Arizona and Nevada have completly different ideas of what machaca is. It is supposed to be dry beef grilled with onions, peppers, tomatoes and eggs. But in Phoenix, it is basically shredded wet beef doused in red or green sauce. Regardless, the Carolina's version was miserable. It was mushy and tasteless and since the thin tortillas could not hold all that beef inside, it turned into a knife and fork thing. I barely ate three bites of the mess and some fat was also discovered lurking in that meat.  Not good.\nSame thing with the quesadilla. Due to the tortilla being so thin, the cheese overwhelmed the item turning it into a cheese wafer. If I want Machaca, I'm heading back to Nevada next time to a state that knows the true definition of the dish."}

{"review": "As far as chain restaurants go, Chang's is pretty good. Of course, that's not saying a whole lot.

The one item on the menu really worthy of praise is the Oolong marinated Sea Bass. When prepared properly it's delicious, but even this dish can be hit or miss. The first few times I tried it the fish was perfectly seared, crispy on the outside and buttery soft in the center. The last time I ordered the Sea Bass, it tasted so different... almost like it was steamed instead of seared. Not crisp, just sort of mushy. 

The rest of the menu items I have tried have just been alright, not bad but not great. Lettuce wraps were a bit bland, spare ribs were rubbery, egg rolls were mediocre.

The servers mixing up their own style of sauce can be fun, the new mini desserts are a nice touch, there's a full bar. The Vietnamese crab salad is good, I think it is a seasonal irem.

Overall there are just so many better, authentic options in Vegas.  My advice, get out and explore."}

{"review": "What a hidden gem. I say \"hidden\" because before Friday, I didn't realize how good of a museum this place is. Liz and I took the day off from work to do some \"touristy\" Madison things - hit some museums, the zoo, and a brewery tour. The museum did not disappoint.

Admission consists of a suggested donation of $4 per adult. We immediately made our way to the fourth (top) floor so that we could work our way from the top down. 

Each floor was themed and featured excellent exhibits that were well presented, well lit, and well documented. There were plenty of informative videos to compliment the prose. 

We encountered several groups of school kids on field trips; it was never a problem or a distraction. The museum guides kept the groups in good order.

So, whether you're from Wisco or if you have visitors from out-of-state, take a few hours and check out the Wisconsin Historical Museum."}

state: {"review": "My mom was in town visiting and decided to treat the entire family to this show. The show was fantastic. It was much better than I had anticipated. It was a lot of fun. They really get the crowd involved and pumped up. I love that you cheer on a king depending on where you are seated. That was fun. I have three boys and they were very involved in the show--even the 18 month old. He cheered right along with the rest of us. The food was good. Okay, it wasn't gourmet. But seeing as they have to serve things that you can eat with your hands, I think it was pretty good. The only thing I didn't like was that the food was not appealing to the kids. For this reason I think they should offer lower priced tickets for kids. But the tickets were $58/person regardless of age. The only exception was for children 3 and under who were allowed to enter for free if they were to sit on a parent's lap and eat off that parent's plate. {"review": "Usually I don't like store-bought cupcakes. I'm a fairly decent baker (okay, I'm good), and my cupcakes are yummy. I make everything from scratch, so I am a tough judge of baked items--especially something as simple to make as cupcakes. Sprinkles, however, is a cut above the rest.

I thought of Sprinkles on my first visit because they have daily words patrons can whisper to get a free cupcake. I was in the area, so I stopped in and whispered the phrase to receive my complimentary red velvet. The sales associate was wonderful, telling me all about the available choices. She even gave me a postcard with all of the flavors so I could plan my next visit. I'm looking forward to peanut butter chocolate day!

I make really great red velvet cupcakes, but this one was just as good! The cream cheese icing was rich and creamy, and the cupcake tasted fresh and crumbly, just like homemade. I was a little disappointed that I didn't take more time to savor it because it was a fiesta for my tastebuds.

At $3.25 each, I won't be frequenting Sprinkles, but it's worth a trip from time to time--especially when I don't feel like baking."}

{"review": "I only give five stars to places that I have been multiple times and been consistently impressed by both the products and the service.  It has to be a place that I would absolutely recommend to anyone, any time.  It has to be, dollar for dollar, a better overall experience.

 Mi Cocina, Mi Pais (their name before some ridiculous chain bearing the same name threatened a law suit) unquestionably fits the bill, and was my regular restaurant during grad school.  I have brought several people to dinner here only to have them leave in gushing awe. The food and service are simply soulful.

It's a challenge to find something that I didn't like there, but I found they are especially good at the slow cooking stuff - stews and the like.  The highlight for me is their sanduche de puerco - a slow cooked pork sandwich served with their incredible and noteworthy aji (a salsa so flavorful and addictive that it deserves a special place of honor).

Mi Cocina, Mi Pais is the sort of place that happens when owners take pride in their food and see their products as a reflection of themselves and their home.  

Recommended."}

{"review": "This place was great! I was in Arizona last year, visiting some friends, and they took me to Oregano's in Gilbert. We got there around 7 pm on a Sunday evening and decided to sit on the patio. I was scared it would still be too hot, but they had air conditioners blasting outside by the table as well as a misty sprinkler system above the patio. Awesome! 

We elected to get a Chicago style deep dish pizza which takes like 45 minutes to make, so we just threw back a couple of ice cold draft beers and the pizza was out in no time. Having the deep dish pizza was a treat because we don't really have too many places that specialize in Chicago style pizza on the west coast. 

The service was outstanding as well. When we were waiting for a table, we went to the bar to get a beer, and the bar tender was on top of his game even though it was chaotic. Our waiter was also very friendly. It turned out that the waiter's fiance was from my home town. Small world. Overall it was a great experience, and I look forward to stopping by again next time I'm in the Phoenix area. 

5 out of 5 stars."}

{"review": "One of the best pizzas I've ever had.

I read a lot of the reviews so I was worried about the service, but I had no problems.  I was the only one in the \"eating area\" so maybe it's hit and miss depending on how busy they are, but the waitress came fast, the food came fast, and she came back often.

I ordered a Wee pepperoni/sausage and it was exactly the type of pizza I like.  The cheese stretches out, the crust has a crispy outer texture but is softer inside, and the sausage is the crumbled kind, not the Domino's type nuggets.  I'm not a huge red sauce fan but I didn't even notice it.

I got the wings (naked) with the suicide sauce on the side.  People are right when they say it's spicy but it doesn't stay with you.  I'm guessing it's habenero.   

The total for the pizza, 10 wings, and a soda was $22.  I managed to get through about half of it and I'm a pretty big eater.

I'm definitely going to go back when I return to Vegas in the future.  Everyone has different tastes in pizza, and if this is the style you like, you're going to love it."}

{"subject": "Night Sky Notes: Leonids, a quiet Moon, and Saturn's rings", "body": "Greetings stargazers,

The Leonid meteor shower peaks on the night of Nov 17-18. With a thin crescent Moon this year, skies should be nicely dark. Expect around 10-15 meteors per hour from a dark site after midnight.

THIS MONTH'S TARGETS
- Saturn: visible in the south after sunset. Its rings appear very thin this year, a rare treat.
- Pleiades: rising in the east by 8pm. Binoculars reveal dozens of stars.

CLUB NEWS
Our next observing night is Nov 14 at Marsh Ridge, weather permitting. Dress warmly, bring a red flashlight, and a thermos.

GEAR CORNER
Thinking about a first telescope? A 6-inch Dobsonian is hard to beat for the price.

Clear skies,
Oliver Prasad, Eastfield Astronomy Society"}

{"subject": "The Tuesday Plate: Quince season, a dumpling crawl, and one very good bakery closing", "body": "Hello, hungry neighbours,

This week's digest from Plate & Pavement.

THE BIG NEWS
Brennig's Bakehouse on Alder Row is closing its doors on 22 November after 14 years. Owner Dilys Brennig says she's retiring to Anglesey to "sleep past 3 a.m. for the first time since 2012." Go and get a loaf of the caraway rye while you can. Her final week will feature a different laminated pastry every day.

WHAT WE ATE
- Little Tamsin's Dumpling House (Corrin Street): the pork and chive pan-fried dumplings are crisp on the bottom and properly juicy. Eight for £7.50. The chilli oil is made in-house and is not shy. 4.5/5
- Fennimore's Pantry: a quince and almond tart that tasted like autumn in a good way. They sell the quince paste separately now.
- The new lunch counter at Ostler & Daughters: skip the soup, order the lentil salad.

DUMPLING CRAWL
Saturday 14 November, 12:00. We'll hit four spots in the Corrin Street area, about 2 hours, roughly £25 all in. Reply to this email to save a place. 12 spots only.

RECIPE OF THE WEEK
Baked quince with honey and bay. Peel, halve and core 4 quinces. Arrange in a dish with 3 tbsp honey, 2 bay leaves, a splash of white wine and 300 ml water. Cover with foil and bake at 160°C for 2 hours until rosy. Serve with thick yoghurt.

See you next Tuesday,
Marguerite
Plate & Pavement

{"subject": "The Quince Issue: jelly, regrets, and a very sticky stove", "body": "Hello again, fellow snackers,

I said I would never make quince jelly a second time. Last autumn it took six hours, ruined a tea towel, and my neighbour Odile still brings it up. And yet here I am, with 4 kg of lumpy yellow fruit from the Marchetti allotment and a stove that now has a permanent amber glaze.

This issue:

1) THE RECIPE: Lazy Quince Paste (membrillo, more or less)
Peel, core, and chop 1 kg quince. Simmer in just enough water until soft, about 35 minutes. Blend, weigh the purée, and add 75% of that weight in sugar. Cook on low, stirring constantly, for 40-50 minutes until it pulls away from the pot. Pour into a lined tin and leave overnight. Serve with salty cheese. Wear long sleeves because the purée spits like an angry cat.

2) WHERE I ATE THIS MONTH
- Tamsin's Hatch (behind the Corn Exchange): the leek and mustard toastie is the best thing I have eaten in 2026. Cash only, closes when the bread runs out, usually 1:30.
- Brindle & Co. Noodle Bar: good broth, but the chilli oil is shy. Ask for the 'real one' and they will bring a small jar from the back.

3) MARKET NEWS
The Saturday market at St. Aldhelm's moves indoors from 14 Nov until March. The cheese van (Wenlow Dairy) will be there, and the woman who sells eleven kinds of pickled walnut has promised a twelfth.

4) READER MAIL
Priya asked whether you can freeze quince. Yes, peeled and cored, in lemon water first. Thank you also to the three of you who told me my 'sourdough starter named Gerald' joke was tired. Gerald has died anyway.

See you in two weeks. Eat something with butter in it.

Marguerite

Monthly notes, November

Dear members,

By now your colonies should be tucked up. If you haven't yet fitted mouse guards, do it this weekend. Mice move in once temperatures drop below about 8 C, and they treat a warm hive like a holiday cottage.

WHAT TO DO THIS MONTH
- Check hive weight by tilting from behind. It should feel heavy. If it doesn't, emergency fondant (not syrup) on the crown board.
- Do an oxalic acid trickle treatment in December during the broodless period. We'll cover this in detail at the next meeting.
- Keep entrances clear of dead bees after storms.
- Resist the urge to open the hive. They are fine. You are not helping.

Monthly Observing Notes - November 2026

Greetings, stargazers.

PLANETS
Saturn is still well placed in the southern evening sky, setting around midnight early in the month. Its rings are quite thin at the moment, tilted nearly edge-on from our viewpoint, so don't expect the classic postcard view. Jupiter rises in the evening and dominates the late-night sky. Mars appears in the pre-dawn east. Venus is lost in the Sun's glare.

METEORS
The Leonids peak overnight on 17-18 November. Expect around 10-15 meteors per hour under dark skies. The Moon is a waning crescent and will not interfere much. Best viewing is after midnight, when the radiant in Leo is high. Dress warmly and bring a reclining chair.

DEEP SKY TARGETS
- M31 (Andromeda Galaxy): high in the evening, visible to the naked eye from dark sites.
- The Double Cluster in Perseus: spectacular in binoculars.
- NGC 457, the 'Owl Cluster' in Cassiopeia: a good one for small telescopes.

SOCIETY NEWS
- Public observing night: Sat 14 Nov, 7 pm, Kettlewell Field. Cloud-cancelled notices go out by 5 pm on the day.
- Monthly meeting: Wed 25 Nov, 7:30 pm. Talk: 'Measuring the Hubble Constant with a Cardboard Tube', by Dr. Anya Voss.
- The 8-inch Dobsonian is available for loan to members. Please sign it out and return it clean.

Clear skies,
Frank Delaney, Newsletter Editor

Dear members,

With the first frost behind us, now is the time to check your hives are winter-ready.

CHECKLIST
- Mouse guards on every entrance by the end of this week
- Heft the hives. A colony should feel heavy at the back. If it feels light, feed fondant, not syrup, now that it's cold
- Strap hives down if you're on the exposed ridge sites
- Ventilation matters more than insulation. Damp kills more bees than cold

VARROA
Oxalic acid trickle treatment is best done in December when the colony is broodless. We will run a hands-on demonstration at the apiary on Saturday December 6. Please bring your own gloves and goggles. Do not skip the goggles.

SOCIETY NEWS
Our honey show raised £412 for the equipment fund. Special mention to Wilhelmina Cho, whose heather honey took best in show for the third year running. Cries of "fix!" were good natured.

MENTORING
We have four new beekeepers without mentors. If you can spare an hour a month, please reply and let me know.

Keep warm, and let the bees alone,
Anders"}

THIS MONTH IN THE SKY
- Leonid meteor shower peaks overnight on 17 to 18 November. Expect around 10 to 15 meteors an hour from a dark site. The Moon will be a thin waning crescent, so conditions are good.

WORKSHOP
Saturday 28 November, 10 a.m. to 4 p.m. Grind your own 6-inch telescope mirror with guidance from Warrick Ibe. Materials £45. Spaces are limited to eight, and no experience is needed.

MEMBERS' PHOTOS

THE HIGHLIGHT
The Leonid meteor shower peaks overnight on 17-18 November. This year the Moon is a thin crescent that sets early, so conditions should be good after midnight. Expect 10 to 15 meteors an hour from a dark site. Dress warmly. Then dress warmer than that.

PLANETS
Saturn is well placed in the southern sky after dusk, with its rings tilted only slightly toward us. Jupiter rises around 8 pm and is bright enough to spot even from town.

DEEP SKY TARGET
Try the Double Cluster in Perseus. It's visible as a fuzzy patch to the naked eye and resolves into hundreds of stars in binoculars.

FROM THE OBSERVATORY
Our public viewing nights run Fridays at 7 pm, weather permitting. We check the forecast by 4 pm and post an update on the website.

BEGINNER TIP

Happy observing,
Nadia Kowalczyk
Edgemoor Amateur Astronomical Society"}

{"subject": "The Fathom Report: deep-sea notes for curious people (Issue 63)", "body": "Welcome back, fathomers.

This issue: a fish with a transparent head, a squabble over seabed mining language, and why we still know more about the surface of Mars than the ocean floor.

THE CREATURE
Researchers from the Aldermoor Oceanographic Institute have released new footage of a barreleye filmed at 800 metres. Its eyes swivel beneath a clear, fluid-filled dome. Yes, really. The clip is 40 seconds long and strangely calming.

THE POLICY
Delegates are still arguing over whether 'precautionary approach' should be binding or advisory in the draft seabed minerals text. Our plain-English explainer is below. No jargon, no sighing.

THE NUMBER
26%. That's the share of the global seafloor mapped to modern high resolution. It was 19% five years ago.

READER MAIL
Solveig from Tromsø asked whether the glowing plankton she saw from a ferry was bioluminescence or sea sparkle. Answer: probably dinoflagellates. Lovely either way.

Until next fortnight, stay curious and keep a little salt on your tongue.

Orla Venning
Editor, The Fathom Report"}

{"subject": "Sky Notes for November – Leonids, a tidy Jupiter, and clear-night forecast", "body": "Eastfield Astronomical Society
Monthly Sky Notes, November

HIGHLIGHTS

Leonid meteor shower: peaks overnight on 17–18 November. This year the Moon is a thin waning crescent, so skies should be decently dark. Expect 10–15 meteors an hour from a dark site after midnight. Face east-ish and give your eyes twenty minutes to adjust.

Jupiter: well placed in the evening, rising in the east by around 8pm and high up before dawn. Even a small telescope shows the four Galilean moons and the dark equatorial bands. Great for beginners.

Saturn: still visible low in the south-west after dusk, though the rings are narrowing as they tilt toward edge-on. A subtle but fascinating change.

SOCIETY NEWS
- Observing night: Saturday 15 November at Pike Hill field, from 7pm, weather permitting. We will confirm by 4pm on the day via the members' list. Bring a flask, a red torch, and an extra layer. Then another extra layer.
- Beginners' workshop: 'Collimating your Newtonian,' Wednesday 26 November, 7:30pm at the library annexe. Bring your scope if you have one.
- The club's 8-inch Dobsonian is available to borrow for members. See Alfonso to sign it out. Please return it with the caps on.

A note on light pollution: the new car park floodlights at the retail park are still too bright. Our letter to the council has gone out and we'll let you know the reply.

Clear skies,
Noor Ibekwe
Observations Secretary, Eastfield Astronomical Society"}

Reader Philippa K. wrote in to say that the steak-and-ale pie at The Gull & Anchor is "structurally unsound." I went to investigate. The pastry lid does slump, but the gravy is so good I did not care. Verdict: bring a spoon.

See you at the market,
Marguerite Olbrecht

Autumn passage is winding down, but the estuary is far from quiet.

HIGHLIGHTS THIS FORTNIGHT
- Around 3,200 wigeon counted on the high tide roost, our best October–November total in six years.
- A juvenile spoonbill lingered near the sluice for four days (last seen Nov 1).
- Two short-eared owls hunting over the saltmarsh at dusk. Best viewed from the east hide at about 4pm.
- Water pipits are back on the creek edge.

VISITOR NOTES
The west boardwalk is closed for repairs until at least the 20th. Please use the east path and stick to marked routes; the roost is sensitive to disturbance.

UPCOMING WALKS
Sat Nov 14, 9am: Beginners' winter wader walk (bring a flask)
Sun Nov 29, 8am: Full tide count, volunteers needed

Please log your sightings on the group's shared sheet. Even common species help.

Happy birding,
Gideon Pryce
Wexcombe Estuary Birdwatching Group"}

{"subject": "Recipe you asked for (finally)", "body": "Hi Auntie Joyce,

Here's the plum cake recipe, as promised. Fair warning: Grandma never wrote down amounts, so I've guessed from memory and from three failed attempts.

- 250g plums, halved
- 180g flour
- 120g sugar (a bit less if the plums are sweet)
- 2 eggs
- 100g butter, softened
- 1 tsp baking powder
- cinnamon, as much as feels right

Bake at 180°C for about 45 minutes, until a knife comes out clean. Plums go face up. If it comes out soggy, you did it right, because that's how hers was.

Tell me how it goes!
Pia"}
